questions.question: Explain the effectiveness of NCLT in resolving company law disputes efficiently.
questions.solution_html:
• The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in India is effective in resolving company law
  • disputes efficiently by providing a specialized forum for adjudicating matters related to company
  • law. It handles cases like disputes between shareholders, oppression and mismanagement, winding
  • up of companies, and more. NCLT aims to provide speedy resolution compared to traditional
  • courts.
questions.final_answer: courts
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is an Abridged Prospectus? Describe its contents and purpose.
questions.solution_html:
• An Abridged Prospectus is a shorter version of the prospectus issued by a company to potential
  • investors when issuing securities. It contains key details about the company and the issue but in a
  • condensed form. Its purpose is to provide essential information to investors for making informed
  • decisions without overwhelming them with full details as in a complete prospectus.
questions.final_answer: decisions without overwhelming them with full details as in a complete prospectus
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain how perpetual succession ensures the continuous existence of an incorporated
questions.solution_html:
• company.
  • Perpetual succession means a company continues to exist despite changes in its members
  • (shareholders or directors). An incorporated company has a separate legal identity from its
  • members. So, even if shareholders or directors die or transfer their shares, the company keeps
  • existing until it's wound up legally.
questions.final_answer: existing until it's wound up legally
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the purpose and importance of the ‘objects clause’ in the Memorandum of
questions.solution_html:
• Association.
  • The objects clause in a company's Memorandum of Association defines the scope of activities the
  • company can undertake. Its purpose is to specify the company's objectives and limit its actions to
  • those stated, protecting shareholders and stakeholders by ensuring the company doesn't engage in
  • activities beyond its stated objectives.
questions.final_answer: activities beyond its stated objectives
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe statutory provisions that allow lifting the corporate veil under the Companies Act.
questions.solution_html:
• Under the Companies Act, 2013 in India, the corporate veil can be lifted in certain situations like
  • fraud, improper conduct, or to determine the true nature of a transaction. Courts may disregard the
  • separate legal entity principle to uncover the reality behind the corporate facade when there's
  • misuse of the corporate structure.
questions.final_answer: misuse of the corporate structure
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the concept of One Person Company (OPC) introduced in the Companies Act, 2013.
questions.solution_html:
• A One Person Company (OPC) is a company with only one member (shareholder). Introduced in
  • the Companies Act, 2013, it allows a single person to incorporate a company, enjoying benefits of
  • limited liability while having full control.
questions.final_answer: limited liability while having full control
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Distinguish between equity shares and preference shares.
questions.solution_html:
• Equity shares give shareholders voting rights and dividends based on company profits. Preference
  • shares have preferential rights to dividends (fixed rate) and repayment of capital but typically don't
  • have voting rights unless specified.
questions.final_answer: have voting rights unless specified
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the procedure for the appointment of directors in a public company.
questions.solution_html:
• In a public company under the Companies Act, 2013, directors are appointed by shareholders
  • through a resolution in a general meeting. The company must follow provisions regarding number
  • of directors, qualifications, disqualifications, and rotational retirement of directors.
questions.final_answer: of directors, qualifications, disqualifications, and rotational retirement of directors
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is meant by membership in a company? Who can become a member?
questions.solution_html:
• Membership in a company refers to being a shareholder. Anyone (individuals, bodies corporate)
  • who agrees to become a member and whose name is entered in the register of members can become
  • a member by subscribing to the memorandum, agreeing to take shares, or by transfer of shares.
questions.final_answer: a member by subscribing to the memorandum, agreeing to take shares, or by transfer of shares
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Question 22
questions.solution_html:
• Qualifications for a company secretary
  • In India, to be appointed as a company secretary, an individual typically needs to be a member of
  • the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI). The qualifications include
  •  Passing the exams conducted by ICSI.
  •  Completing the required practical training.
  •  Being a member of ICSI.
questions.final_answer:  Being a member of ICSI
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Question 23
questions.solution_html:
• Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) importance
  • Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) refers to a company's commitment to operate ethically and
  • contribute to the economic development of society while improving the quality of life of the
  • workforce, their families, and the local community. In today's business environment in India, CSR
  • is important because
  •  It enhances the company's reputation and brand image.
  •  CSR activities can contribute to sustainable development.
  •  Companies in India with a certain turnover or profit are mandated to spend a percentage of
  • their profits on CSR activities as per the Companies Act, 2013.
questions.final_answer: their profits on CSR activities as per the Companies Act, 2013
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Question 24
questions.solution_html:
• Resolution for winding up operations and distributing assets.
  • For a company to wind up its operations and distribute assets among shareholders, a Special
  • Resolution is typically required. This is as per the Companies Act, 2013, where a special resolution
  • needs to be passed by the shareholders for winding up the company voluntarily.
questions.final_answer: needs to be passed by the shareholders for winding up the company voluntarily
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Question 25
questions.solution_html:
• Provisions related to CSR
  • In India, provisions related to CSR are primarily governed by Section 135 of the Companies Act
  • 2013. Key points include
  •  Companies with a net worth of ₹500 crore or more, or turnover of ₹1000 crore or more, or
  • a net profit of ₹5 crore or more during any financial year are required to constitute a CSR
  • Committee.
  •  Such companies need to spend at least 2% of their average net profits of the preceding
  • three financial years on CSR activities.
  •  CSR activities should be in areas like education, healthcare, environment sustainability
  • etc., as specified in Schedule VII of the Act.
questions.final_answer: etc., as specified in Schedule VII of the Act
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
